Title: Verify that the collected amount is tracked under a default user ID when no specific user ID is provided
Preconditions: User is logged into the application and has access to the transaction recording feature. No prior transactions have been recorded under the default user ID 'USER001'.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Record Transaction' screen. 2. Enter a valid transaction ID (e.g., 'TXN12345'). 3. Enter a transaction amount of $500. 4. Submit the transaction without specifying a user ID. 5. Navigate to the 'Transaction Summary' screen.

Test Data: Transaction ID: TXN12345, Amount: $500
Expected Result: The 'Transaction Summary' screen displays a collected amount of $500 under the default user ID 'USER001'.

Title: Verify that all users' transaction amounts are incorrectly aggregated under a single hardcoded user ID, leading to potential unauthorized access to another user's collected amount
Preconditions: Two distinct user accounts exist in the system, each with at least one recorded transaction. The system tracks collected amounts per user.
Steps:
1. Log in as User A and record a transaction of 500.00.
2. Log out.
3. Log in as User B and record a transaction of 300.00.
4. Log out.
5. Log in as User A and view the collected amount summary.
6. Log in as User B and view the collected amount summary.

Test Data: User A ID: any valid user ID (e.g., USER002), User B ID: any other valid user ID (e.g., USER003), Transaction amounts: 500.00 and 300.00
Expected Result: User A sees only their own collected amount (500.00). User B sees only their own collected amount (300.00). Neither user sees the other's transaction data or a combined total.

Title: Verify that a user cannot infer another user's collected amount by manipulating transaction inputs or observing system behavior
Preconditions: Two distinct user accounts exist in the system. The system tracks collected amounts per user.
Steps:
1. Log in as User A and record a transaction of 1000.00.
2. Log out.
3. Log in as User B and attempt to record a transaction with an amount that would exceed a typical daily limit (e.g., 10,000.00).
4. Observe the error message or system response.
5. Attempt to record a transaction with a negative amount (e.g., -100.00).
6. Observe the error message or system response.

Test Data: User A ID: any valid user ID, User B ID: any other valid user ID, Transaction amounts: 10,000.00 and -100.00
Expected Result: User B's transactions are rejected with generic error messages that do not reveal User A's collected amount or any system limits. No sensitive data (e.g., other users' balances, internal thresholds) is exposed in error messages or logs.
